what_it_does: Harvesting energy from vibrating piezoelectric materials (like a crystal that generates voltage when squeezed) can power wireless sensors, but the circuit must automatically track the optimal operating point to extract maximum power. Existing methods either interrupt energy flow while measuring (FOCV) or slowly tweak power (perturb-and-observe), losing energy either way. This paper presents a biased-SECE interface (a hybrid switching circuit) with geometric-mean-computational MPPT—a maximum-power-point tracker that computes the geometric mean of two voltages without interrupting energy flow. The result: 99.9% of theoretical maximum power, tracked 8.75 times per voltage change, enabling 9.3 times more total energy extracted compared to naive approaches.
